target.title: fix(xai): gate server-side tools to xAI models only
target.body:
Closes #97621

## What Problem This Solves

The xAI extension's `code_execution` and `x_search` tool factories use `ctx.activeModel?.provider` to decide whether to expose xAI-billed tools. The original guard `ctx.activeModel?.provider && ctx.activeModel.provider !== PROVIDER_ID` uses `&&` which is **fail-open**: when `activeModel` is missing or its `provider` field is undefined, the guard evaluates to `undefined` (falsy), and the tool is exposed to non-xAI sessions — potentially billing the xAI account from other providers' use.

## Why This Change Was Made

Changed both guards to `ctx.activeModel?.provider !== PROVIDER_ID`, which is **fail-closed**: when the provider is undefined, unknown, or any value other than "xai", the guard returns `null` and the tool is hidden. The tool-construction path must positively prove the active model is from xAI before billing the xAI account.

## Evidence

### Vitest factory-level tests (10 new tests)

The factory gating is tested directly through the exported `createLazyCodeExecutionTool` and `createLazyXSearchTool` functions — covering the real factory path at `extensions/xai/index.ts:118`, not a copied guard.

```console
$ npx vitest run extensions/xai/index.test.ts --no-coverage

 ✓ |extension-providers| ../../extensions/xai/index.test.ts (26 tests) 514ms
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > exposes the tool when activeModel.provider is xai
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is non-xAI (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is undefined (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel is missing entirely (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is empty string (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > exposes the tool when activeModel.provider is xai
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is non-xAI (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is undefined (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel is missing entirely (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is empty string (fail-closed)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

### Guard comparison

| Scenario | Old guard (fail-open) | New guard (fail-closed) |
|---|---|---|
| provider = "xai" | Tool exposed | Tool exposed |
| provider = "openai" | null (hidden) | null (hidden) |
| provider = undefined | **Tool exposed** (leak!) | null (hidden) |
| no activeModel | **Tool exposed** (leak!) | null (hidden) |

### Not tested

- Live multi-provider tool resolution with xAI API keys (requires running gateway)

## Merge Risk

**Low**. The change only tightens an existing guard — the xAI tool path already required passing credential checks. The fail-closed behavior is the safer default for provider-billed resources.
